A 21-year-old male patient comes to establish primary care after a recent emergency department visit
for abdominal pain that has resolved. A CT scan during that visit revealed bilateral kidney cysts. He
reports low back pain with radiation to the flanks following recent heavy lifting, which is exacerbated by
exercise. His medical history includes a successfully treated urinary tract infection eight months ago.
His vital signs show: temperature 37.0 ºC (98.6 ºF), pulse 72/min, respiratory rate 15/min, and blood
pressure 151/95 mm Hg. Physical examination reveals bilateral paraspinal muscle tenderness in the
lumbar spine, but no costovertebral angle tenderness and non-palpable kidneys. The left first toe
shows warmth, swelling, erythema, and tenderness on palpation. Abdominal examination and

urinalysis are normal. Which clinical finding would warrant genetic testing for this patient? Answer
Choices: (A) Normal urinalysis despite symptoms (B) Flank pain (C) Monoarticular arthritis of the
first metatarsal joint of the foot (D) Bilateral kidney cysts before age 30 (E) Family history of kidney
disease (F) Musculoskeletal pain with exercise (G) Recent onset of symptoms (H) Elevated blood
pressure (I) Non-palpable kidneys (J) Prior urinary tract infection
 A. Musculoskeletal pain with exercise
B. Recent onset of symptoms
C. Normal urinalysis despite symptoms
D. Bilateral kidney cysts before age 30
E. Monoarticular arthritis of the first metatarsal joint of the foot
F. Non-palpable kidneys
G. Family history of kidney disease
H. Flank pain
I. Prior urinary tract infection
J. Elevated blood pressure
